title: Two Indian-Origin Delta Residents Named as Victims in Targeted Surrey Walmart Shooting
excerpt: Gaganpreet “Garry” Rehal, 23, and Sukhjeet Kaur, 24, were shot outside the Newton Walmart on November 15; investigators cite indicators of organised crime and are seeking dashcam video.
body:
• Police have identified the two people killed outside a Surrey Walmart on November 15 as Gaganpreet “Garry” Rehal, 23, and Sukhjeet Kaur, 24, both residents of Delta, British Columbia.
  • Investigators believe the shooting was targeted and say it carries indicators of organised crime; no suspect has been named and the motive is still under investigation.
  • A burnt four-door sedan found after a vehicle fire on Princess Drive is believed to have been involved in the homicide.
  • Police are asking anyone with dashcam video from the area between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on November 15 to call the IHIT information line at 1-877-551-4448.

Canadian homicide investigators have identified the two people shot dead outside a Walmart store in Surrey, British Columbia, on the night of November 15 as Gaganpreet “Garry” Rehal, 23, and Sukhjeet Kaur, 24. The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT) said both victims were residents of the neighbouring township of Delta, and that it released their names to help advance the investigation.

Surrey Police Service officers and paramedics found the two with gunshot wounds near 88 Avenue and 124 Street in the Newton neighbourhood shortly after 10:30 p.m. on November 15, according to IHIT. Both were pronounced dead in hospital.

A targeted attack, investigators say

IHIT said it believes the shooting was targeted and that there are indicators of organised crime, though the motive remains under investigation. The release said Rehal had previous police interactions related to weapons and firearms offences, while Kaur had limited known contacts in Canada. Investigators are working with the victims' families to establish their activities in the period leading up to the shooting.

"This shooting has left two families grieving the loss of two lives lost too soon."

— Sgt. Freda Fong, Integrated Homicide Investigation Team, quoted by CBC News

The burnt car and the search for witnesses

About twenty minutes after the shooting, at 10:51 p.m., a vehicle fire was reported in the 9700-block of Princess Drive in Surrey. Investigators recovered a burnt four-door sedan that they believe was involved in the homicide, and are working to identify the occupants who fled the scene, IHIT said.

IHIT is seeking witnesses and dashcam video from either area between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday, November 15. Anyone with information can call the IHIT information line at 1-877-551-4448 or email ihitinfo@rcmp-grc.gc.ca.

The investigation comes weeks after British Columbia's Provincial Extortion Task Force announced charges against two men, Pardeep Singh and Saveer Khan, both 22, in connection with a shooting at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Surrey and a separate attack on a home that injured a woman, according to IANS. Police have not linked that case to the Walmart shooting.

What is not yet known

Police have not named any suspect, announced an arrest, or confirmed a gang affiliation. Sgt. Freda Fong said extensive work is under way to pursue all available leads and identify those responsible. For Surrey and Delta's large South Asian community, the case is the latest in a series of targeted shootings in the Lower Mainland that police have linked to organised crime; what distinguishes this one, investigators say, is that one of the two people killed had, in their words, limited known contacts in Canada.
